note.explanation: Living things are made of cells. Cells carry out the functions needed for life. Most cells are too small to see without a microscope, although a few are large enough to see with the naked eye.
examples: The ostrich egg cell is large enough to be seen with the naked eye.
A cell is like a city: different structures do different jobs, while the nucleus directs the cell's activities.
note.checkAnswer: Cells are the building blocks of living organisms and carry out the functions needed for life.
note.simple: Cells are tiny building blocks that make up living things and do the work needed to keep them alive.
note.checkQuestion: What is the basic unit of life?
note.title: 3.1 Cell
steps: Remember that the cell is the basic unit of life.
Explain that living organisms are made of cells.
Add that cells carry out the functions necessary for life.
note.answer: The cell is the basic unit of life.

examTips: For a short-answer question asking what a cell is, write the textbook definition: “The cell is the basic unit of life.”
If asked to explain why cells matter, state that they are the building blocks of living organisms and carry out the functions necessary for life.
For a question about cell size, remember that most cells cannot be seen with the naked eye, but the section gives the ostrich egg cell, Acetabularia and a giant Amoeba as examples that can be seen.
Use the cell-city comparison carefully: the nucleus directs activities, while other cell structures carry out different jobs.

example.question: Using the cell-city comparison, explain how different structures in a cell carry out different jobs.
example.answer: A cell is like a busy city: some structures produce energy, some process and transport materials, others remove or break down wastes, and the nucleus directs the cell's activities.

explain.title: The cell is the basic unit
explain.body: “The cell is the basic unit of life.” Just as bricks are the building blocks of a house, cells are the building blocks of living organisms, including plants, animals and humans.

explain.title: Cells do the work of life
explain.body: Cells are the units that carry out all the functions necessary for life. They are complex, even though most are very small.

explain.title: Most cells are microscopic
explain.body: Most cells cannot be seen with the naked eye. The section gives the ostrich egg cell, Acetabularia and a giant Amoeba as examples large enough to be seen.

explain.title: A cell is like a city
explain.body: Different cell structures have different jobs. The nucleus directs the cell's activities, like a city's government giving instructions.

mistakes: Do not define a cell only as a tiny object; include that it is the basic unit of life.
Do not say that every cell can be seen with the naked eye. Most cells are too small to see without a microscope.
Do not say that only plants have cells; the section names plants, animals and humans as living things made of cells.
When using the city comparison, do not mix up the nucleus's directing role with the jobs of structures that transport materials or remove waste.
